contexts.text: An offering (or present) () = worship; (for) all the sacrifices were called offerings. Illustrated. AC 355. AC 1171.
The offering of Judah () = worship from celestial love; and the offering of Jerusalem = worship from spiritual love.
An offering in a clean vessel () = a representative of the external man relatively to the internal. That which brings the present is the internal man.
A present for Esau his brother () = Divine things initiated into celestial natural good... A present = initiation... because it was made to secure goodwill and favour.

The presents made in old times signified various things... Those given to kings and priests on approaching them, signified initiation; and those offered upon an altar, worship. For all the sacrifices, in general, of whatever kind, were called presents (or offerings); but, in special, the meat-offerings... for meat-offering, in the Original Language, means a present.
That presents were given to kings and priests, on approaching them. Illustrated. AC 4364, Explained.
The presents given to priests and kings were as if [given] to Jehovah.
That the presents which were sent = initiation. Illustrated. Here, their presents are called initiation.
Refusal to accept a present insinuates affection. Signified.
The fundamental of charity is to act rightly and justly in everything relating to any duty or function.

Make a present descend to the man () = to obtain grace... In the Ancient representative Church it was customary to give something as a present to the judges, and afterwards to the kings and priests, when they approached them; and this was even commanded. The reason was that the presents which they gave them represented such things with man as ought to be offered to the Lord when He is approached, which are the things which are from freedom... From this must man give a present to the Lord when He is approached...
These presents were initiations; and initiations are to obtain grace.
They prepared a present () = insinuation; for a present = to obtain grace. AC 5675.
The office of the Angels is to inspire charity and faith, etc., etc.
The neighbour is loved when anyone discharges his function rightly for the good of others...
which is greater, the gift or the altar which sanctifieth the gift? ()... By the gift, or sacrifice, were signified the things of faith and charity which are from the Lord.

Thou shalt not receive a present () = aversion for any gain whatever; (for) a present = everything worldly which is loved; whether it be opulence, dignity, reputation, or anything else which is flattering to the natural man. These things, in general, are called gain; and, in the internal sense, are meant by a present which blinds and perverts.
Because a present blinds those whose eyes are open () = that gains cause truths not to appear... As also in, A present blinds the eyes of the wise ().

Not to see My faces empty (); that is, without a present, = testification for the reception of good, and thanksgiving; for the presents which were offered to Jehovah = such things as are offered to the Lord by man from the heart, and are accepted by the Lord. It is with presents as with all the deeds of man. Explained... The like is the case with presents, in that it is the will in them which is regarded by the Lord. Hence it is, that by the presents offered to Jehovah... are signified such things as are of the will... Illustrated.
(Thus) the presents offered to the Lord were testifications of such things as are offered with the heart; which are the things of faith and charity.
The gifts offered by the wise men. Explained.
To bring a present, and to bring a gift () = the good of love and of faith. ( = to worship. AE 406:9.)
It is the goods of love and of faith in the Lord which... are meant by an offering to Jehovah ().
As by a present offered to Jehovah is signified the good of love and of faith, it is said that they bring to Jehovah an offering in justice ().
See Gift.
To offer a present in oil to the king () = to worship Satan from evils. A present in oil is a meat-offering.
The office of (priests) is called the priesthood.
They shall send presents to one another () = consociation through love and friendship... For a present consociates; because it produces love, and makes friendship.
Those who had been judges of friendship and of presents. Described.
The office given them is to prepare vermilion wherewith to bedaub the faces of harlots.
It is at their pleasure to bestow, these presents either before betrothal, or after it. Explained.
See Functions.
Illustration and instruction... belong to their office.
According to the amplitude of the function...
The Lord has... sent me to this office.
To offer a gift upon the altar () = all Divine worship, because with that nation Divine worship consisted principally in offering burnt-offerings and sacrifices. AE 391:20.
To be enriched with these (Knowledges) is signified by to bring a present ().

As presents capture minds, and consociate, it was customary in ancient times to give presents to a priest and a prophet, and also to a prince and a king, when they approached them. Illustrated. And therefore also the offerings upon the altar... and also the meat and drink-offerings were called presents. Illustrated. This was because external presents signified internal or spiritual presents; those, to wit, which proceed from the heart, and which are therefore of the affection and the faith. And as through these conjunction is effected, therefore by presents, in the spiritual sense are signified conjunction, when predicated of God; and consociation, when predicated of men.
A gift upon the altar = the worship of the Lord from love and charity.
That the Lord will do these things gratis, is signified by not for price nor present ().
The daughter of Tyre shall send a gift () = worship by those in the Knowledges of truth.

By ministries, are meant priesthoods and their duties; by functions, are meant various offices which are civil; by employments, are meant works, such as those of artificers; and by offices, are meant various studies, businesses, and domestic-servantships. Of these four consists the commonwealth, or society.
That all offices and employments, regarded as to goods of use, make a form which corresponds to the heavenly form. General article.
Everyone there is in some ministry, function, office, or employment...
That in this form everyone is a good of use according to the extension of his office or employment. General article.
That... if (such a man) sincerely, justly, and faithfully performs the work which belongs to his office and employment, he becomes a form of charity. Chapter.
Those who perform [the duties of] their employments solely for the sake of the necessaries of life; or of a name; or a salary. Described.
